newsitem.title: GREECE: AGROTICA MAY BE OBSTRUCTED BY FARMERS' MOVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: AGROTICA MAY BE OBSTRUCTED BY FARMERS' MOVEMENT.

text.p: This year's Agrotica farming exhibition of machinery, equipment and supplies is scheduled to start on January 29 in Athens but could be obstructed by a farmers' movement on January 28, organisers said in a statement.
Helexpo which is the exhibition's Greek organiser has expressed concerns as farmers have said they will disrupt public services in central Greece a day before the exhibition.
Farmers have threatened to renew on February 4 a strike they staged in December by blocking national roads to protest against tight incomes and tax policies.
Some farmers' union representatives have adopted a milder stand on the issue of strikes, saying that both sides should seek a fruitful dialogue.

"Our demands are fair but I think that we must continue to negotiate with the government as the satisfaction of most of our demands seems to be already under way," a Panhellenic Confederation of Farm Federation Unions representative said.
The 1997 Agrotica will host 675 Greek and 777 foreign exhibitors from January 29 to February 2. It is considered as one of the three biggest farming exhibitions in Europe, Helexpo's statement said.
Sales prospects of Greek farming machinery are good. sales rose 16 percent in 1996, said Pavlos Kontellis, president of the Federation of Importers and Representatives of Farming Machinery.
